record.title: Anthropic revises its Usage Policy with explicit rules for deceptive campaigns and high-risk physical actions
record.summary: Anthropic’s updated Usage Policy, marked effective November 12, 2026, adds explicit requirements for users connecting its models to hardware capable of high-risk physical actions: a qualified person must be able to observe and stop equipment, which must enter or hold a safe state if the person intervenes or service connectivity is lost. The revision also has a separate prohibition on deceptive campaigns and artificial activity, including fake personas, concealed sponsorship and networks of ostensibly independent sites. Comparison with Anthropic’s archived September 15, 2025 policy confirms the physical-action controls are new to this document. This is a provider usage policy, not a law; enforcement and resulting safety outcomes are unverified.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic says the update consolidates deceptive-campaign rules that were previously distributed across other policy sections and clarifies rules for longer, more independent work.

evidence_gaps.description: The revised Usage Policy is future-effective; this activation did not inspect real enforcement, customer compliance or changes in incident outcomes.

brief.importance_rationale: If applied as written, explicit controls for model-connected high-risk physical actions and clearer prohibitions on deceptive campaigns could affect frontier-model deployment practices across user products. The consequence is notable, but this is one provider’s usage policy; enforcement outcomes and any reduction in incidents are not established.
limitations: The updated policy is marked effective November 12, 2026; this activation occurred before that date.
This is Anthropic’s provider usage policy, not legislation or a regulator requirement.

brief.title: Anthropic revises its Usage Policy with explicit rules for deceptive campaigns and high-risk physical actions
brief.why_it_matters: The policy sets clearer deployment conditions for agent-connected equipment in high-risk settings and more explicitly covers coordinated deceptive campaigns, potentially affecting how developers design monitoring, stop controls and user-facing applications around Anthropic models. The text establishes the provider’s stated requirements and effective date, but not compliance, enforcement quality or a reduction in real-world incidents.
